extracted.intended_audience: NLP / ML researchers and practitioners who want to study or model peer reviews using the PeerRead dataset
extracted.subtask_description: Using the PeerRead dataset (NAACL 2018) of paper drafts, accept/reject decisions, and textual peer reviews for NLP experiments such as aspect prediction and acceptance prediction. Includes setup and data-download instructions and the paper citation to use when publishing results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset composition and coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The dataset consists of over 14K paper drafts with corresponding accept/reject decisions from top-tier venues (ACL, NIPS, ICLR) and over 10K textual peer reviews for a subset of the papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The data is structured into sections per venue or arXiv category (e.g., ./data/acl_2017, ./data/arxiv.cs.cl_2007-2017). Use these sections to select venue-specific subsets for experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train/dev/test splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Each section is further split into the train/dev/test splits (the same splits used in the paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should use the provided splits for experiments to ensure comparability with the paper's results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and partial-download requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to licensing constraints some sections of the data are not included in the repository; instead the repo provides instructions for downloading those sections (e.g., ./data/nips_2013-2017/README.md).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the per-section README/instructions to obtain restricted data; be aware that some parts require separate downloads and may be subject to additional license/consent constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported tasks / model targets
rubrics_metrics.description: The repository supports experiments for aspect prediction (predicting review aspects) and for predicting whether a paper will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ./code/README.md for model code and reproduction notes. Use the dataset fields appropriate to each task (text of reviews, labels, accept/reject decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup and reproducibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Run ./setup.sh at the root of the repository to install dependencies and to download some of the larger data files that are not included in the repo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided setup script to reproduce authors' environment and to obtain any auxiliary files; check requirements.txt and code/README.md for further reproducibility instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When using the dataset in publications, cite the NAACL 2018 paper: Kang et al., 'A Dataset of Peer Reviews (PeerRead): Collection, Insights and NLP Applications'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The README includes the BibTeX entry to include in papers. Respect the authors' citation request when publishing results derived from this data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent / opt-in provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some data (e.g., official reviews) were included only when authors and reviewers opted in during the official review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of provenance and consent metadata when analyzing or releasing derived data; acknowledgements note cooperation with conference chairs and platforms (softconf.com, openreview.net, arxiv.org, semanticscholar.org).
